children: TRex Bio filed for an initial public offering and plans to list on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the ticker “TRXB.” The clinical-stage biotech develops immunoregulatory medicines targeting tissue regulatory T cells, led by a TNFR2 agonist in Phase 1b for atopic dermatitis. Proceeds will fund Phase 2 studies for its lead asset, an initial clinical study for a second program, and general corporate purposes.

TRex Bio is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company developing immunoregulatory medicines that augment tissue regulatory T cells (Tregs) to restore immune balance and promote tissue repair in autoimmune and inflammatory diseases. Its proprietary Deep Biology platform integrates human tissue biology, computational mapping, and functional assays to identify targets and design translational strategies grounded in tissue-level Treg mechanisms.

Lead candidate TRB-061 is a selective TNFR2 agonist Fc-fusion protein designed to expand and activate tissue Tregs without stimulating proinflammatory cells. TRB-061 is in a Phase 1b study in moderate-to-severe atopic dermatitis, with topline data expected in mid-2027, and the company plans Phase 2 trials in atopic dermatitis and alopecia areata. A second wholly owned program, TRB-071, is a CD30 agonist antibody intended to activate Tregs and modulate inflammatory signaling; it is in IND-enabling studies with a Phase 1 trial planned for the first half of 2027. TRex Bio also has an ongoing collaboration with Eli Lilly based on a program (TRB-051) initially identified on its platform.
: Atopic dermatitis impacts ~16 million U.S. adults and ~225 million people globally; IBD affects ~3 million in the U.S. and is expected to surpass 10 million worldwide by 2032.
: Increasing prevalence of autoimmune and inflammatory diseases, with rising demand for targeted, durable therapies beyond broad immunosuppression.
: TRex Bio focuses on tissue Treg augmentation to restore immune balance and promote tissue repair, aiming for durable disease control.
: Developers of AD, IBD and AA therapies including biologics (e.g., IL-4/13, IL-23, anti-TNFs) and JAK inhibitors; emerging Treg-directed and IL-2 pathway approaches.
: Shift from broad immunosuppression to precision immunoregulation; emphasis on tissue-level biology, biomarkers, and durable remission.
: Not applicable (clinical-stage biopharma with no commercial products)
: Headquarters in South San Francisco, California
: U.S.-based operations; clinical activities in Australia and New Zealand for early trials
: Collaboration with Eli Lilly (TRB-051 advanced toward Phase 2a in lupus with cutaneous involvement); prior Janssen collaboration terminated in 2025
: Approximately 60 full-time employees as of August 31, 2026
: No collaboration revenue recognized in 2025 or the six months ended June 30, 2026 (2024 collaboration revenue: $39.1 million)
: Operating loss of $37.8 million in 2025; operating loss of $31.0 million for the six months ended June 30, 2026
: Net loss of $34.8 million in 2025; net loss of $29.3 million for the six months ended June 30, 2026
, Chief Executive Officer and Chair - Over 35 years at Eli Lilly across regulatory, clinical and corporate development; led Lilly New Ventures and global regulatory submissions for Evista and Forteo.

, Chief Medical Officer - 20+ years in immunology clinical development; prior roles at Biora Therapeutics, Human Immunology Biosciences and Genentech/Roche; former Stanford clinician.
